substitutions.name: the in-process host over an in-memory link
substitutions.reason: Production runs the session host as a separate purlis-app process over a socket; the scenario host runs the host's own code in-process over the in-memory link (`hostedsessions::tests::in_memory`), so the socket, the process boundary and the host's own environment are not exercised.

substitutions.name: the Tauri mock runtime
substitutions.reason: The window's `Planes` are managed by `tauri::test::mock_builder()`; the real webview, its event loop and the ACL over real IPC are not exercised (the ACL is `ipc.rs`'s own tests).

substitutions.name: the hand-built kit in place of `Composes::shipped()`'s discovery
substitutions.reason: `Composes::shipped()` finds its `purlis` beside the executable, its plugin in Tauri's resource folder and its git hooks in the real data folder; the scenario host names each itself (`scenarios::host::Kit`), so that discovery is not exercised.

substitutions.name: the Claude Code leg's variables: the stand-in model's address and key, and two that keep its start-up traffic in
substitutions.reason: The leg's chats start from the keep-list, and `ANTHROPIC_*` is among the credentials it drops: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (the stand-in model's loopback address), ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (a literal that is no credential), CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC and DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER (Claude Code's unsandboxed main process does not use purlis's proxy, so its own start-up traffic would go out) are named in the test plane's `charter.local.toml` `[chat_env] pass`, with their values in the host's environment. A person's chat is given none of them (T1.1-10, `scenarios::real_leg::added`).

substitutions.name: the first-run state seeded for Claude Code on macOS
substitutions.reason: purlis seeds a Claude Code profile's first-run state (onboarding, the trusted folder, the approved key) for the Linux wrap alone (`claude_wrap.rs`); the Claude Code leg writes it itself in the sandbox-only profile's own folder (`scenarios::real_leg::seed_first_run`), as a person who had answered the questions would have, so an interactive start does not stop at them.

substitutions.name: the Codex leg's API key, and the model provider its launch words name
substitutions.reason: The leg's chats start from the keep-list, and `OPENAI_*` is among the credentials it drops: OPENAI_API_KEY (a literal that is no credential) is named in the test plane's `charter.local.toml` `[chat_env] pass` with its value in the host's environment, and Codex is told its model provider (the stand-in model's loopback address, over the Responses API, with no retry) in `-c` words beside purlis's own on its launch line, as the recordings are made (`scenarios::real_leg::launch_words`, T1.1-53). A person's chat is given neither.

substitutions.name: the OpenCode leg's inline configuration and its start-up switch
substitutions.reason: The leg's chats start from the keep-list: OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT (the whole configuration, naming the stand-in model's loopback address as its one provider, over Chat Completions, with a literal that is no credential as its key) and OPENCODE_DISABLE_AUTOUPDATE are named in the test plane's `charter.local.toml` `[chat_env] pass`, with their values in the host's environment (`scenarios::real_leg::opencode_config`, T1.1-53). A person's chat is given neither.

substitutions.name: the stand-in model's loopback port, granted to a wrapped chat
substitutions.reason: A chat purlis wraps reaches no host the project does not list, and no model is called in the leg: the stand-in model's loopback port is granted to the chat (`sandbox::local::grant_port`), as the recordings' chats are granted theirs, where a person's chat reaches its vendor through the proxy with the host the project lists (`Scenario::starts_real`, T1.1-53).

substitutions.name: OpenCode's commands end by saying their own exit status
substitutions.reason: OpenCode's Bash tool result carries no exit status, and a cell reads whether a command ran and how it ended: the leg asks OpenCode for each command inside a group that ends by echoing its own status, so the cells read the same exit in every harness. A person's chat is asked no such thing (`scenarios::real_leg::command_for`, T1.1-53).
